author: Associated Press
description:
Prosecutors had said Caleb Flynn staged a home invasion after shooting his wife while he was having an affair

  • Caleb Flynn, former Ohio pastor, found guilty of wife’s murder

A former Ohio music pastor who once appeared on American Idol was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole on Monday after a jury convicted him of murdering his wife while he was having an affair.

Prosecutors said Caleb Flynn, 40, staged a home invasion in February after shooting Ashley Flynn, a 37-year-old schoolteacher and volleyball coach. Flynn claimed she was killed by a burglar.

Continue reading...
title: Former American Idol contestant and pastor sentenced to life in prison for murdering his wife

author: Jason Burke in London and Stephanie Kirchgaessner in Washington
description:
Police and security agencies in multiple countries scramble to piece together background and intentions of Hamam al-Hammami

Investigators believe that the co-pilot who tried to take control of a plane from Dubai to Tel Aviv last week originally planned his attack for July but postponed the hijacking, possibly because a friend was among the crew, regional and Israeli officials have said.

The evidence of prior planning suggests that Hamam al-Hammami, 29, may have specifically sought employment with an airline that flew to Israel in order to carry out the attack on last Wednesday’s flydubai ‌flight FZ1073, experts believe.

Continue reading...
title: Flydubai co-pilot originally planned attack for July, investigators believe

author: Guardian staff
description:
The Last Week Tonight host looked into the issues plaguing the Secret Service, from lack of funds to an insular culture

On the latest Last Week Tonight, John Oliver looked into the Secret Service, tasked with protecting the US president among many other things. “Agents have a high-stakes job, and that’s what makes it so worrisome that by all accounts the Secret Service is heading into what might be one of its most challenging periods yet,” the host noted, referring to 2028, or what some agents have called “Armageddon”, as the service will be tasked with staffing the LA Olympics and Paralympics, the annual United Nations general assembly and the two presidential candidates and their families during the election.

No wonder, then, that the Secret Service recruited none other than action movie impresario Michael Bay to direct a recruitment ad f
title: John Oliver on the overstretched, underfunded Secret Service: ‘Actively reckless’

title: Brazil’s presidential election and a green river: photos of the day – Monday

author: Jack Larkin
description:
My brother said I was terrible at mulching; he was right. But before tearing up my contract, he imparted some words of wisdom

In early 2020 in Canberra, I left my job in human resources. Ironically the constant onboarding and offboarding of employees made me realise no one ever stays in the same job forever.

By the time winter rolled around, it was Covid lockdowns. I had grown a scruffy beard and turned my bedroom in my mother’s house into a man cave, complete with empty beer cans, a TV blaring sport and a glowing gaming setup in the corner.

Continue reading...
title: A job that changed me: I mulched city parks in the dead of winter – I was not cut out for manual labour or working with family

author: Daniel Gallan
description:
The hosts’ stunning Test victory was overshadowed by the scale of national angst felt in Australia after the team’s ball tampering

For South African cricketers, administrators and supporters, the most surprising aspect of the Sandpaper scandal was not that it happened. After all, the ball had been suspiciously reverse-swinging during the first two Tests of that ill-fated series in 2018. The atmosphere had turned febrile after a stairwell bust-up between Quinton de Kock and David Warner in Durban and after supporters directed misogynistic abuse at Warner and his family in Gqeberha. Nathan Lyon had promised before the tour to “head-butt the line” of what was acceptable. Darren Lehmann, then Australia’s coach, came from an old school where bullying was sugar-coated with the phrase “mental disintegration”.

No, what surprised South Africans most was the scale of the fallout, and how one tiny piece of sandpaper could cause so much national angst.
title: Sandpaper made Australia the story in 2018 while South Africa’s achievement faded into irrelevance

author: Katharine Gammon in Los Angeles
description:
An international symbol for the city, the sign is also hallmark of the region’s environmental richness

Atop Mount Lee, in the heart of Los Angeles, the wind is quiet. Two red-tailed hawks sail above, barely flapping as they coast the thermal air like surfers on a wave. Standing beside the giant letters of the Hollywood sign, the city seems peaceful. On a clear day, blocks and blocks of homes unfold beneath and the skies reveal sights all the way to Catalina Island – 10 miles out, across the Pacific.

That’s the beauty seen from the Hollywood sign.

Continue reading...
title: Snakes, bobcats, mountain lions: the secret animal world beneath the Hollywood sign

author: Ranjana Srivastava
description:
Our relationships with pets matter to wellbeing. But concern for an animal’s welfare can also become a practical barrier to healthcare

“Doctor, do you know I have a little dog?”

My team exchanges a glance. It’s my turn today.

title: What happens to a dog when its owner can’t leave hospital? | Ranjana Srivastava

author: Interviews by Chris Broughton
description:
‘When I couldn’t do the spitting scene, Sean took me aside and said: “Ron, if you don’t actually spit in my face, we’ll be here all day.” So I let one fly – and kept having to redo it’

I read an article about a curious book that had great reviews in Italy, a murder mystery about monks in the middle ages fighting for the fictional missing part of Aristotle’s Poetics. I said: “This is for me.” Since childhood, I had been fascinated with medieval and religious architecture, and Aristotle’s Poetics is my favourite literary work.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I spat in Sean Connery’s face 16 times’: Ron Perlman on making The Name of the Rose

author: Sam Hockley-Smith
description:
Sphere, Las Vegas
The first night of a new residency is an immersive plunge into the band’s visual world that showcases the depth of their catalog

Las Vegas’s Sphere takes on the characteristics of whatever it’s advertising on its exterior. Depending on when you look, you might see Orbi, the Sphere mascot, winking at you, or an ad for one of their Wizard of Oz showings, or maybe a roiling mass of red flames and shocks of lightning announcing the arrival of Metallica for their residency Life Burns Faster. Looking at it feels like staring at the end times. It’s like a huge black hole, sucking in the jittery sun blasted energy of Vegas and transmuting it into an ominous ode to the renegade titans of thrash, but, you know, an older, wiser, therapized version of the band.

This is the first night of Metallica’s 24 show residency, and it features the return of their “no repeat” format, meaning they p
title: Metallica review – metal titans on fine form in spectacular rarities-focused show

author: Eric Berger
description:
Culture of silence and fears of exclusion means aviation workers less likely to seek help for mental health issues

Pilots and air traffic controllers in the US could soon have an easier time achieving a healthy mental altitude – a move with implications for the safety of air travel in America.

The US Senate recently approved bills aimed at encouraging aviation professionals struggling with a mental health condition get treatment.

Continue reading...
title: Senate-approved bills aim to ease burden on pilots amid mental health ‘stigma’

author: Sidney Blumenthal
description:
The vice-president’s recent remarks seek to maintain a posture of strength while they inadvertently expose political realities

JD Vance has parachuted into the midterm election campaign on a rescue mission in a new guise: a risk management consultant. Speaking in the flat language of the expert hired to identify threats, weaknesses and losses affecting a business’ reputation, he has presented his executive summary for limiting vulnerabilities and a scenario for averting disaster.

“There’s a lot of good that’s been done, but there’s a lot of work left to do,” he informed his clients on 15 September about the words to use. “Give us another chance, or give us another couple of years, to continue to work on the amazing things that we’ve been doing for the past two years.” He turned the focus to harm reduction rather than total agreement and then shifted the equation to a negative bina
title: Vance wants voters to ‘give us another chance’. But he is cornered | Sidney Blumenthal

author: Sam Jones in Madrid
description:
Spanish PM is hoping to shore up his fragile mandate by tapping into public anger over country’s housing crisis

  • Europe live – latest updates

Spaniards will head to the polls on 29 November – months before schedule – after the country’s socialist prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, announced a snap general election on Monday morning. The vote, which will be Spain’s fifth general election in 10 years, is likely to be dominated by growing anger over the housing crisis

Continue reading...
title: Will Pedro Sánchez’s gamble to call snap general election in Spain pay off?

author: Erika Hayasaki
description:
Norma Bowe, 68, was flung to the ground at Delaney Hall, the infamous New Jersey detention center. She sees her lawsuit against ICE as one step towards justice

Norma Bowe pressed a stethoscope against the 10-year-old’s chest, listening to her lungs.

It was Memorial Day outside Delaney Hall, an immigration detention center in Newark, New Jersey. The child, worried about her father locked inside, was hyperventilating.

Continue reading...
title: This nurse was assaulted by ICE – and it was caught on video. Now she wants her day in court

description:
President to visit Grand Island as his plan to allow more foreign beef imports proves unpopular in agriculture-rich state

Sign up for the Breaking News US email

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

Donald Trump will be in Nebraska later today, campaigning alongside Republican senator Pete Ricketts, in an attempt to salvage the GOP’s dwindling midterms campaign.

The White House has defended a newly hired press aide who posed for a holiday photograph in 2021 wearing a “Fuck Joe Biden” T-shirt and holding a rifle. Beni Rae Harmony, the new assistant White House press secretar
title: Trump heads to Nebraska in attempt to shore up GOP’s midterm vote – US politics live

author: Steven Band, as told to Deborah Solomon
description:
A beloved family pet, she is also the best employee ever, brilliant at her rescue work. If everyone could be more like Poppy, the world would be a better place

When we picked up a nine-week-old black labrador from a couple just outside Callander, Scotland, I had no idea that she would soon be an employee of mine. Poppy became the family fur baby and we realised early on how clever and empathic she is. I work as a Special Operations Response Team paramedic and we decided to involve her in my search work in 2021 when she was only a year old because we knew it would play to her strengths. She took to it immediately.

Poppy and our team of dogs look for missing people. My colleagues and I then provide any medical assistance needed. She is trained to search without needing to smell someone’s scent from an item such as clothing. During training, we hide our volunteers along the riverbank, in the woods, beside lochs and canals, and set the dogs off. They have to fin
title: The pet I’ll never forget: Poppy the curious, clever dog – who searches for missing people

author: Emma Beddington
description:
From microcheating to quiet quitting to weaponised incompetence, new terms to describe relationship failings are abundant. But that doesn’t mean there’s not space for some more ...

Are you committing “attention infidelity”? The New York Times alerted me to this expression, coined by the public opinion researcher Daniel Cox in a new book on the “crisis of human connection”. It’s exactly what you’d expect: failing to focus fully on your partner because you’re indulging in what the NYT calls, rather judgily, “the banal distraction of dead-eyed scrolling”. Who are you calling dead-eyed? This reel of an armadillo in a paddling pool has my animated attention!

Surely we’re all a bit attention-unfaithful – only saints don’t sometimes absent-mindedly thumb through
title: Is your partner on their phone and ignoring you? I’ve got a buzzword for that

author: Peter Bradshaw
description:
This biopic of Sergiu Celibidache, the renowned Romanian conductor who refused all recordings, is a sturdy labour of love directed by his son

Here is an old-fashioned biopic from central Europe that is also a labour of love on the part of its director: a little stolid and stately, yes, but robustly made, heartfelt and high-minded, with workmanlike performances and decent visual effects work. It is the story of the Romanian conductor and composer Sergiu Celibidache, a brilliant musician who became renowned among musical connoisseurs in the years following the second world war for his unique and uncompromisingly purist belief – derived from his Zen Buddhist studies – that music should never be recorded. He believed that LPs and CDs were inert and dead, and that music had to be experienced live, in the passionately authentic present.

The director is the musician’s son, Serge Ioan Celebidachi, and as an older man in his rural French retirement, he is played with unsubtly qu
title: The Yellow Tie review – John Malkovich gives major hauteur as legendary record-hating maestro

author: Steven Greenhouse
description:
Our ‘genius’ president is revealing his ignorance of economics, fueling concerns about the threat he poses to the world

Donald Trump recently made a bold claim about his abilities, writing on Truth Social: “The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!”

But in the days before and after that post, Trump made one mind-boggling statement after another, including one that raised the possibility of cutting off all trade with dozens of the US’s trading partners. The president’s statements had many experts questioning not just his intelligence, but also whether he – and the outlandish policies he was proposing – were a clear and present danger to both the US economy and the world economy. Public respect for Trump’s economic sense has fallen
title: Trump’s recent statements on the economy are even more bonkers than usual | Steven Greenhouse

author: Zoe Wood
description:
Natural History Museum and British Museum among cultural institutions leveraging collections and exhibitions

They are often free to visit but museums are bolstering their finances by putting their stamp on everything from upmarket hotel suites to trendy jumpsuits and virtual reality experiences.

Forget buying a T-shirt. If you can afford the “from £724” price tag, you can spend the night in the Natural History Museum family suite at the Park Plaza London Riverbank hotel, which has an interior inspired by the museum’s founder, Sir Richard Owen, complete with Tyrannosaurus rex bunk beds.

Continue reading...
title: From hotel suites to virtual reality, museums turn to licensing deals as costs rise

author: Sian Cain
description:
Alejandro G Iñárritu’s film may be about to become one of the biggest bombs Hollywood has ever seen – but it is destined to be re-evaluated with time

  • This article contains spoilers for Digger

I feel for film critics, I really do. Tom Cruise’s latest film Digger put them in an impossible position: you can’t really talk about it without spoiling what makes it, in my eyes, a masterpiece. Or completely terrible – as many, many critics have argued over the last week, without being fully free to say why.

That is not their fault: media screenings around the world opened with a plea from Warner Bros to not spoil the film’s central reveal. This seems like it may have been a misstep, because curiosity and Cruise alone were clearly not enough to get bums on seats. Digger is
title: Tom Cruise’s Digger has flopped spectacularly – but I think it is a misunderstood masterpiece

author: Stephen Burgen in Barcelona
description:
Nine years on from a failed independence push, former president Carles Puigdemont will find times have changed

After years of legal wrangling, Spain’s constitutional court is expected to remove the last obstacle to the return of the former Catalan president Carles Puigdemont after nearly nine years in exile this week.

Puigdemont fled in 2017 to avoid being jailed for his part in the failed and illegal independence push for which nine of his colleagues were imprisoned on sentences of up to 13 years, although all were released within three years.

Continue reading...
title: Exiled separatist leader is likely to return to a very different Catalonia

author: Stephanie Convery
description:
Fitness influencer, 46, faces court on Monday after his arrest in Noosa at the weekend

The fitness influencer and reality TV star Sam Wood has been charged in Queensland with domestic violence offences.

The personal trainer and star of the third season of the Australian version of the reality TV show The Bachelor was charged on Sunday and spent the weekend in police custody after an alleged incident on Saturday night.

Continue reading...
title: Former Bachelor star Sam Wood charged with domestic violence

author: Tom Phillips and Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
description:
Far-right challenger and son of disgraced ex-president Jair Bolsonaro will now face leftwing president in runoff vote

Brazil’s presidential race will go to a second round after the far-right candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, beat the incumbent leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, but failed to secure the outright majority he needed to avoid a runoff.

With more than 98% of votes counted, the 45-year-old son of the disgraced former president, Jair Bolsonaro, had won 47.3%, meaning he will now face a 25 October showdown with his 80-year-old rival. Lula received 44.8%.

Continue reading...
title: Brazil’s presidential race to go to second round as Flávio Bolsonaro leads incumbent Lula
